title: IV cannula insertion
what: A nurse puts a thin, soft tube into a vein. The needle is taken out right away, and only the plastic stays in the vein. Medicines and drips go through it without new injections.
why: When you need many injections or drips, before surgery or a scan with contrast dye, and in hospital.
tell_doctor: Allergy to plasters, latex, or antiseptics
If an arm must not be used, for example after lymph node removal or with a dialysis fistula
If your veins have been hard to find before

prepare.title: Water
prepare.text: If you are allowed to drink, have some water ahead of time. Your veins fill better.

prepare.title: Warmth
prepare.text: Warm hands make veins easier to see. If your hands are cold, warm them up.

bring: Clothes with a sleeve that is easy to roll up
steps: The nurse chooses a vein, usually on the hand or forearm
A band is tied above it and the skin is wiped
A needle with a tube goes in. This is a quick prick
The needle is removed, and the tube stays in the vein
The cannula is closed with a cap and taped in place
feel: A prick, like during a blood draw
After that, you barely feel the cannula
When medicine goes in, your arm may sometimes feel cool
after: Do not get the cannula wet, and do not pull on it
You can use your arm, but do not bend it much if the cannula is at the elbow
Usually the cannula stays for up to 3 to 4 days, then it is changed or removed
Removal is quick and almost painless. A cotton pad is put on the spot
red_flags: Pain, swelling, or redness around the cannula or along the vein: tell the nurse right away
Fluid from the drip goes under the skin and your arm swells: ask for the drip to be stopped
A fever or chills: tell your doctor

faq.q: Does the needle stay in the vein?
faq.a: No. The needle is removed right away. Only a soft plastic tube stays in the vein.

faq.q: How long can a cannula stay in?
faq.a: Usually up to 3 to 4 days. If you have pain or redness, it is removed sooner.
